sources.citation: Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, archive.org, SIL OAI harvest (held by the project), Bing/DuckDuckGo searches for 'Gudu' Chadic
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Gudu-specific publication, thesis or SIL report found; web searches return only the Wikipedia stub (which cites nothing beyond Ethnologue). Kraft 1981 has no open scan. SIL archive search page could not be reached by automated download; not in the Internet Archive.

sources.citation: Roger Blench website, Chadic directory (rogerblench.info/Language/Afroasiatic/Chadic/*), the Internet Archive's index listing of 174 archived documents
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Gudu or Bata-group document exists in the archived tree (Central Chadic folders: Baka, Bura, Kirya, Lagwan Kotoko, Mofu, Muyang, Ouldeme, Vame). Live domain is now hijacked (gambling site).

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT 375. Utrecht.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Table 3 (Introduction, p.13 of the source list) gives 'Gudu [gdu] Bata none', i.e. no source at all for Gudu; sec. 3.3.1 lists Gudu among the twelve Bata-group languages. Nothing on Gudu stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd ed., entry 157 Gudu
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Entry 157: Gutu, Gudo; Song LGA, ~5 villages; 1,200 (1971); Chadic Biu-Mandara A, Bata group; Source(s) 'L. Jacobson wordlist'; Refs. Meek (1931: I.124). Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: lexibank/kraftchadic (CLDF digitisation of Kraft 1981), raw/ + NOTES/TRANSCRIPTION/FORMS/README
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 437 tone-marked Gudu forms only; Kraft's Notes are not digitised; no mention of stress in the dataset notes.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and reference table for gudu1250 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists exactly 4 references (Meek 1931; Kraft 1981; Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994; Haruna 2005), all typed overview/wordlist/ethnographic; no grammar, sketch or phonology; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Haruna, Andrew. 2005. The endangered languages issue in Northern Nigeria: a Chadic perspective. Borno Museum Society Newsletter 62/63: 7-32.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Only post-1994 reference Glottolog attaches to Gudu; a sociolinguistic overview, unlikely to describe stress but may cite unpublished Nigerian theses on Gudu.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Dymitr Ibriszimow. 1994. Chadic Lexical Roots, 2 vols. Berlin: Reimer.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Comparative root lists incorporating Kraft's Gudu data; no stress information expected, listed only because Glottolog attaches it to Gudu.

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, vol. III ("Biu-Mandara" et al.). Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde, Serie A, 25. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. GUDU section: cover page, tentative phonemic inventory, Notes (consonant notes 1-17, vowel notes incl. no. 7 '(stressed?) variant of /a/', length note), 434-item wordlist (p. ~75ff).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only phonological description of Gudu in existence; its vowel notes contain the sole (tentative) mention of stress; a full read of the Notes would settle whether Kraft/Jacobson say anything about accent or tone placement.

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria, vol. I, pp. 124ff ('The Gudu'; Kumbi Gudu). London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in (archive.org lending); the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: Oldest record of the language (ethnography + vocabulary); Meek's vocabularies occasionally carry accent marks; needed to rule Gudu in or out and for the Gudu/Gombi dialect question.

sources.citation: Jacobson, Leon. n.d. Gudu wordlist (unpublished; cited as 'Source(s) L. Jacobson wordlist' in Blench 2012 Atlas entry 157; Jacobson is also the analyst of Kraft's Gudu list)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: May be the underlying field notes for Kraft's Gudu entry and could carry stress/tone annotations; not known to be deposited anywhere.
